source_policy.owasp_content: Identifiers and titles only; control and residual-risk text is VALO-authored.

risks.title: Prompt Injection
controls: Candidate content cannot mint authority
Exact action authorization and scope binding
Instruction-bearing untrusted memory is quarantined
risks.residual_risk: Adaptive multimodal injection coverage and portfolio-wide channel testing remain incomplete.

risks.title: Sensitive Information Disclosure
controls: Scope and purpose binding
Opaque credential handles
No secrets in compiled runtime profiles
risks.residual_risk: Authorize-before-retrieval, redaction and log-sensitivity enforcement are not yet proven portfolio-wide.

risks.title: Excessive Agency
controls: Deterministic pre-execution authorization
Fresh authority and exact capability scope purpose binding
One-shot permit and replay prevention
High-impact approval and multi-hop reauthorization
risks.residual_risk: Cross-repository composition is not yet proven by one end-to-end harness; Stage 1 closes this.

risks.title: Supply Chain
controls: Model lifecycle and provenance records
Skill hash and source binding
Planned exact-artifact admission gate
risks.residual_risk: Exact digest and version admission for all live models, tools, skills, MCP servers and adapters is not yet mandatory.

risks.title: Data and Model Poisoning
controls: Fail-closed memory admission
Provenance and policy binding
Canonical-memory promotion requires validation and approval
Evidence and reality checks for consequential action
risks.residual_risk: Training and RAG poisoning detection and repair remain broader than current admission controls.

risks.title: Unbounded Consumption
controls: Rate limiting and cost accounting exist
Budget contracts exist
Stage 2 adds atomic hard enforcement for spend, fan-out and recursion
risks.residual_risk: Hard execution-bound resource reservation and recursive fan-out enforcement are not yet proven.

risks.title: Misinformation
controls: Required evidence and reality validation
Verified prior outcomes may gate recursive execution
Receipts separate claims from observed outcomes
risks.residual_risk: VALO does not claim to determine truth of arbitrary model prose; coverage is for consequential reliance.

risks.title: Hidden Context Exposure
controls: Compiled profiles contain no secrets
Credentials use opaque handles
Hidden prompts are not authorization boundaries
risks.residual_risk: Context minimization, redaction and leakage testing are not proven across every runtime and log surface.

risks.title: Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
controls: Retrieved content cannot expand action scope
Memory and provenance admission limits persistence of poisoned content
risks.residual_risk: Vector index ACLs, tenant isolation, authorize-before-retrieve and embedding-model admission remain incomplete.

risks.title: Improper Output Handling
controls: Model output is proposal data not authority
Permit binds exact action payload
Gateway validates bindings before effect
risks.residual_risk: Application-specific encoding, escaping and parser safety remain application and PEP responsibilities.

risks.title: Agent Goal Hijack
controls: Purpose and scope remain authority-bound despite manipulated goals
Untrusted memory cannot silently become instruction
risks.residual_risk: Adaptive goal-hijack testing across modalities remains incomplete.

risks.title: Tool Misuse & Exploitation
controls: Tool capability and resource scope are explicit
Every consequential tool call requires fresh REHT clearance and one-shot permit
risks.residual_risk: Stage 1 will prove cross-stack composition with real contracts.

risks.title: Identity & Privilege Abuse
controls: Principal actor and issuer bindings
Child profiles only narrow
Revoked authority cannot be overridden by skill or tool metadata
risks.residual_risk: Identity-provider integration remains environment-specific even though the execution boundary is deterministic.

risks.title: Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
controls: Provenance and model lifecycle evidence exist
Skill source and hash binding exists
Stage 4 will require exact artifact admission
risks.residual_risk: Live-use admission is not yet uniformly bound to exact artifact digest and version.

risks.title: Unexpected Code Execution (RCE)
controls: Containment attestation and execution-path binding
Direct egress deny-by-default
Tools remain behind governed execution boundary
risks.residual_risk: Sandbox and containment wiring must be proven mandatory across all execution substrates.

risks.title: Memory & Context Poisoning
controls: External and AI-derived instruction-bearing memory is quarantined
Canonical promotion requires validated memory and human approval
Action is reauthorized at consequence boundary
risks.residual_risk: Cross-agent memory propagation and all RAG stores are not yet covered by one conformance suite.

risks.title: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
controls: A2A and MCP are transport only and cannot create authority
Stage 3 adds integrity-bound anti-replay message envelope
risks.residual_risk: Cryptographic message integrity, sender and recipient binding and replay resistance are not yet VALO-wide invariants.

risks.title: Cascading Failures
controls: HALT and revocation exist
Rate limiting and circuit-breaker components exist
Stage 2 adds recursive and fan-out hard limits
risks.residual_risk: Recursive depth, cumulative fan-out and budget exhaustion are not yet hard-enforced end-to-end.

risks.title: Human-Agent Trust Exploitation
controls: Protected and high-impact actions require explicit gate evidence
Approval freezes exact action and execution requires re-clearance
risks.residual_risk: Human-interface rendering and approval-fatigue controls remain product and UI responsibilities.

risks.title: Rogue Agents
controls: Worker self-report cannot mint authority
Execution receipts are authoritative evidence of external effect
Prior outcome can be required and verified
risks.residual_risk: Stage 1 must prove fabricated completion is rejected without a matching receipt across the full stack.
